author: Staff reports, Foster's Daily Democrat
title: ConvenientMD awards scholarships to 11 healthcare students - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff reports, Foster's Daily Democrat ,
1 days ago Naomi Panjaitan of Dover High School is one of 11 high school seniors from Maine, New Hampshire and Massachusetts have been awarded scholarships from ConvenientMD to support their pursuit of healthcare careers.
The program awarded a total of $20,000 in scholarships, according to a community announcement. Six students received $2,500 scholarships, while five received $1,000.
The scholarships are part of ConvenientMD's annual Student Scholarship Program, which aims to invest in the next generation of healthcare professionals. This year, the program received more than 500 applications, which were reviewed by a committee of ConvenientMD team members.
ConvenientMD scholarship winners The 2026 scholarship awardees are:
Yacine Abderrahim, Manchester Central High School, Manchester, New Hampshire Evan Babcock, John Bapst Memorial High School, Glenburn, Maine Morgan Barry, Nashua High School North, Nashua, New Hampshire Isabelle Chaffee, Essex North Shore, Peabody, Massachusetts Lauren Jordan, Noble High School North, Berwick, Maine Brooklynn Lamke, Lenox Memorial High School, Pittsfield, Massachusetts Addisyn Brown, Lynn Vocational and Technical Institute, Lynn, Massachusetts Danica Carlberg, Leominster High School, Leominster, Massachusetts Madison Hannan, Camden Hills Regional High School, Lincolnville, Maine Anushri Mishra, Shrewsbury High School, Shrewsbury, Massachusetts Naomi Panjaitan, Dover High School, Dover, New Hampshire Program aims to strengthen healthcare workforce Since launching the program in 2022, ConvenientMD has awarded more than $76,000 to students pursuing healthcare careers, according to the announcement. The program is one of several initiatives the company uses to support healthier communities through educational initiatives, community partnerships and accessible healthcare services.
ConvenientMD operates 51 urgent care clinics across New Hampshire, Maine and Massachusetts, as well as five primary care clinics in New Hampshire and Maine, with a sixth opening in Maine later this year.
"The dedication and compassion demonstrated by this year's applicants give us great confidence in the future of healthcare across New England. We are proud to support these students as they take the next step in their educational journeys," said Ray Wahl, chief executive officer of ConvenientMD.
